```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# load most recent County Health Rankings data
final_data <- read.csv("flu_vac_data.csv") # dataset created in eda_memo
df <- final_data |> 
  select(fips, state_fips, name, state, flu_vac, rural, pcp_ratio, income, 
         some_college, uninsured_adults, non_eng = Non_Proficient_English)
```

Research question: How do county-level characteristics explain variation in annual county-level influenza vaccination rate among Medicare fee-for-service enrollees?

Primary Data: County Health Rankings full data - published 2025 (2022 data)
Secondary Data: County Health Rankings supplemental data - published 2026 (2023 data)

## Correlation Matrix
Check for colinearity problems. Nothing too bad, r=0.63 between income and some_college is the highest.

```{r echo=F}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4

library(corrplot)

cor_mat <- df |>
  select(rural, pcp_ratio, income, some_college, uninsured_adults, non_eng) |>
  cor(use = "complete.obs")

corrplot(cor_mat,
         method = "color",
         type = "upper",
         addCoef.col = "black",
         number.cex = 0.8,
         tl.col = "black",
         tl.srt = 45,
         diag = FALSE)
```
## Q-Q Plots
Full model will be: lm(flu_vac ~ rural + pcp_ratio + income + some_college + uninsured_adults + non_eng, df).
First, let's check the residuals by making a simple model for each individual predictor.
```{r echo=FALSE}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8

vars <- c("rural", "pcp_ratio", "income", "some_college", "uninsured_adults", "non_eng")

op <- par(mfcol = c(4, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1), cex.main = 0.9)

for (i in seq_along(vars)) {
  formula_str <- as.formula(paste("flu_vac ~", vars[i]))
  m <- lm(formula_str, data = df)

  plot(fitted(m), resid(m),
       xlab = "Fitted values", ylab = "Residuals",
       main = paste("flu_vac ~", vars[i], "(CHR)"))
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

  qqnorm(resid(m), main = paste("Q-Q:", vars[i]))
  qqline(resid(m))
}

par(op)
```
Transforming the ones that look the most problematic:
```{r echo=FALSE}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8

vars <- c("rural", "log(pcp_ratio)", "log(income)", "some_college", "log(uninsured_adults)", "log(non_eng+0.001)")

op <- par(mfcol = c(4, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1), cex.main = 0.9)

for (i in seq_along(vars)) {
  formula_str <- as.formula(paste("flu_vac ~", vars[i]))
  m <- lm(formula_str, data = df)

  plot(fitted(m), resid(m),
       xlab = "Fitted values", ylab = "Residuals",
       main = paste("flu_vac ~", vars[i], "(CHR)"))
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

  qqnorm(resid(m), main = paste("Q-Q:", vars[i]))
  qqline(resid(m))
}

par(op)
```
